resources.string: BBBot plays Block Blast on its own. It reads the screen, decides where the pieces go and drags them there.
BBBot needs its accessibility service to see the screen and to move the pieces. Switch on “BBBot” in the accessibility settings.
A small BBBot panel appears on top of Block Blast.
The choice applies the next time the bot is started.

Wait after every clear until the score stands still, so that the record shows what each piece earned. The bot then needs five to six seconds per clear. Switched off, it only waits for rare clears whose worth is not known yet. Applies the next time it is started.

Switched off, the bot stops as soon as the pieces no longer all fit and leaves the last pieces to you. Switched on, it places what still fits, which ends the game, and goes on with the next game. It does not yet get past the screens and ads the game shows in between by itself; it keeps pictures of them to learn from. Applies the next time it is started.
Lets a combo go sooner to keep the board open. Fewer points in simulation, and no game lost.
The setting that scored best in simulated games.
Defends a long combo at a still higher cost to the board. No more points in simulation, and more games lost.
Lets BBBot play Block Blast: it takes screenshots while the game is in front and drags the pieces onto the board. BBBot does not read the contents of other apps and sends nothing anywhere.
